title: Flexible and expeditious assay for quantitative monitoring of alpha-amylase and amyloglucosidase activities
author: Oliveira, Pinheiro, et al.
materials: The use of a suitable volumetric scale for the assay was also an important concern for our development work. Hence, we kept the same volume ratio of the original method but we increased the assay to a total volume of 3.00 mL according to our requirements, which were defined by the specifications of the US probe used to study the effect of US in the activity of amylolytic enzymes [7,8]. This also means that the volumes could be easily adjusted in order to match the requirements of each particular enzyme analysis or study. Although the small volume (100 μL) used in the original formulation of the assay [5] is an interesting option to minimize reagent consumption and waste disposal, the high temperatures that these enzymes can be submitted may pose problems of volume control caused by evaporation, which may have negative impact in the precision and accuracy of the method. Furthermore, by performing the assay on a volume scale compatible with eppendorfs or vials, it is also possible to easily transfer the sample other subsequent experimental steps (e.g. centrifugation). We adopted this strategy to separate the solid particles that remained after the hydrolysis of different pure starches mediated by amyloglucosidase (glucose yield protocol, step 5).

steps.title: Prepare soluble starch solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve soluble starch by first adding it to cold deionized water, stir until partially dissolved, then add hot deionized water while stirring until fully dissolved, keep stirring while the solution cools to obtain a clear, non‑cloudy solution.

steps.title: Prepare triiodide (KI/I₂) solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the required amount of potassium iodide (KI) in water, then add solid iodine (I₂) and place the mixture in an ultrasonic bath until I₂ is completely solubilised, forming the triiodide reagent.

steps.title: Scale assay to 3 mL total volume
steps.instruction: Set up the amylase/amyloglucosidase activity assay using the same reagent volume ratios as the original method but adjust all volumes so that the final reaction mixture volume is 3.00 mL, which fits standard eppendorf or vial formats.

steps.title: Adjust HCl volume for glucose‑yield assay
steps.instruction: When using a pure starch substrate for the amyloglucosidase glucose‑yield protocol, stop the reaction by adding 200 µL of HCl (instead of the original 750 µL) to maintain the buffering capacity of the GOPOD reagent.

steps.title: Prepare concentrated sodium malate extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 134.1 g malic acid, 70 g NaOH, and 58.4 g NaCl in 900 mL deionized or ultrapure water; add 6.0 g CaCl₂·2H₂O and stir until fully dissolved; adjust the pH to 5.4 with dropwise addition of 4 mol L⁻¹ NaOH or HCl; optionally add 1.0 g sodium azide as preservative; finally dilute the concentrate 200‑fold (e.g., mix 50 mL concentrate with 950 mL water) to obtain the working 1 M sodium malate buffer pH 5.4.

steps.title: Extract α‑amylase from wheat flour
steps.instruction: Weigh 3.0 g wheat flour into a 50 mL flask, add 20.0 mL of the diluted malate buffer (pH 5.4), vortex vigorously, then place the flask in a temperature‑controlled water bath at 40 °C for 15–20 min with occasional swirling; continue with steps 4–8 of the amylolytic enzyme activity assay, and determine enzyme activity within one hour of extraction.

steps.title: Perform starch‑iodine assay measurement
steps.instruction: Dilute each starch standard or sample with 150 µL ultrapure water, add 50 µL of the KI/I₂ triiodide reagent, transfer the 250 µL mixture to a well of a cylindrical flat‑bottom microplate, and record the absorbance at 580 nm (ensuring absorbance values remain ≤ 1).
